note: Critical CSS inlines a per-request critical CSS file into the head and loads other CSS async. Config object critical_css.settings (has schema, but NO config/install defaults, so it does not exist until saved): enabled (bool), dir_path (string, must start with '/', relative to active theme, no '..'), excluded_ids (newline-separated entity ids), enabled_for_logged_in_users (bool), preload_non_critical_css (bool). Form route critical_css.settings at /admin/config/development/performance/critical-css (permission: core administer site configuration). File match order ends in default-critical.css. Disabled on admin routes and AJAX; disabled for logged-in users unless enabled_for_logged_in_users. Medium/hard cases write/read the critical_css.settings config; baseline is 'config absent', so cleanup deletes the object.

evals.prompt: How do I switch on the Critical CSS module and tell it which directory holds my critical CSS files? Name the config object/keys and the settings page path.
evals.expected_output: Enable it on /admin/config/development/performance/critical-css (route critical_css.settings) and set the 'Critical CSS base directory' (dir_path, must start with '/', relative to the active theme). Config keys live in critical_css.settings: enabled, dir_path, excluded_ids, enabled_for_logged_in_users, preload_non_critical_css.

evals.prompt: Inside the critical CSS directory, what filenames does critical_css look for to match a page, and what is the final fallback filename if nothing more specific exists?
evals.expected_output: It tries, most specific first: {entity_id}.css, path-{path}.css, {path}.css, path-{path_info}.css, {path_info}.css, {bundle}.css (e.g. article.css), and finally the fallback default-critical.css.

evals.prompt: On which requests does critical_css never inline critical CSS, even when enabled - think admin pages, AJAX, and logged-in users?
evals.expected_output: It is disabled on admin routes (for users who can view the admin theme), on AJAX/XHR requests, and for authenticated users unless enabled_for_logged_in_users is on; entities listed in excluded_ids are also skipped.

evals.prompt: Critical CSS is configured on this site. Inspect the live critical_css.settings configuration and report the directory path (relative to the theme) where it looks for critical CSS files.
On this site, Critical CSS has been told to skip processing for certain entity ids. Read the live critical_css.settings and report which entity ids are excluded from critical CSS.
evals.expected_output: critical_css.settings excluded_ids lists 42 and 99 (one id per line).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, configure the Critical CSS module so it is enabled and looks for critical CSS files in the directory '/css/critical' (relative to the active theme). Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: In critical_css.settings set enabled = true and dir_path = '/css/critical' (via the settings form or \Drupal::configFactory()->getEditable('critical_css.settings')->set('enabled', TRUE)->set('dir_path', '/css/critical')->save()).

evals.prompt: Critical CSS is already on for this site, but I need node 7 to load its CSS the normal way instead of using critical CSS. Configure Critical CSS to exclude entity id 7 from critical CSS processing, and apply it to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Add 7 to critical_css.settings excluded_ids (one id per line), e.g. \Drupal::configFactory()->getEditable('critical_css.settings')->set('excluded_ids', "7")->save(), or enter 7 in the 'Exclude entity ids' textarea on the settings form.
